name: galaxy-mcp: a local upload goes through Loom's uploader, never MCP upload_file
description: Loom registers galaxy-mcp with toolExposure { upload_file: hidden }: local-path upload over MCP times out on large files, and galaxy_upload_local_file (resumable TUS) replaces it. With pi's built-in MCP that hiding is a config field rather than adapter code, so a regression would quietly hand the model mcp__galaxy__upload_file again. The prompt names a file in the workspace, which is exactly the request that tool would have answered. The upload also has to land: Loom's uploader must return a success and the submission hook must register its job, which pins the details-reading path of the capture for a live upload rather than a replayed one. The history is named with the loom-eval- prefix so --galaxy-cleanup can purge it. The timeout sits above the uploader's own 600s ingest bound, so a slow queue on the shared server ends in the tool's verdict rather than the runner's SIGTERM.
inputs: Create a new Galaxy history named exactly `loom-eval-upload-{{RUN_ID}}`, then upload the local file `counts.tsv` from this folder into that history as a tabular dataset. Tell me the new dataset's id when it's done. This is a quick data-staging request, so skip the plan and don't edit the notebook.
